title: the mountain of herbs
hook: the smell of a mountain on the wind, an army rising, and a peak put back

segments.voice: Yesterday: the mountain of herbs. The plants hid, so Hanuman lifted the whole peak and flew it south. Did you step back and take in the whole picture? Today, he lands. Day six hundred fifty.

The monkeys who are still conscious see it first: a light in the northern sky, coming fast. Then they hear Hanuman's roar, and they roar back, weak and astonished. He sets down over the battlefield with a mountain in his hands, trees and rocks and all, glowing in the dark. And before anyone has picked a single leaf, something happens that nobody planned. The wind carries the scent of the herbs out over the field.
screen: `A LIGHT IN THE NORTH.` → `HANUMAN'S ROAR.` → `THE SCENT ON THE WIND.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki, that's all it takes. The smell of the healing herbs drifts over the fallen, and they rise. Rama and Lakshmana breathe in, and the arrows come out of them, and their wounds close. All around them the monkeys and bears get up, shaking themselves, as if they'd been asleep. Valmiki goes further: even monkeys who had been killed come back to life. He also notes something about the other side. The rakshasas who had died didn't rise, because Ravana had ordered his dead thrown into the sea, so the enemy wouldn't see how many he'd lost. A king hiding his losses, and so cutting his own people off from healing: Valmiki lets that detail speak for itself. Then Hanuman does something the famous picture doesn't show. He picks up the mountain again, flies it all the way back north, and sets it in its place in the Himalaya. Then he returns to the camp. The peak was borrowed, not taken. He doesn't keep the prize, or put it on display. The emergency is over, so the mountain goes home. There's a later telling, in the Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas, where Bharata shoots Hanuman down over Ayodhya as he carries the mountain. In Valmiki the trip is uninterrupted: north, south, north again, and back before the battle starts.
screen: `THE SCENT ALONE HEALS.` · `EVEN THE FALLEN RISE.` · `RAVANA HID HIS DEAD.` · `THE MOUNTAIN GOES HOME.` · then, large: `BORROWED, NOT TAKEN.`

segments.voice: Sit and breathe in slowly through the nose, as if the scent of something good were on the air. Let each breath in be a little healing, for one tired place in the body. Then think of something you borrowed in a crisis: someone's time, their help, their patience. Is there anything to put back? Hold that kindly. Breathe in. Breathe out. The bell holds the time.
The mountain of herbs. Its scent alone lifts the fallen army, and when the work is done, Hanuman carries the peak back home to the Himalaya.
Your line: the mountain of herbs. Today, give back one thing you borrowed in a hard time: time, a favor, a thank-you. Day six hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Hanuman's flight with the herb mountain is recited and sung in devotion to him, in Valmiki's telling and in later ones such as the Ramcharitmanas.

fork.setup: you're Hanuman. the army is healed and the mountain is sitting on the battlefield. what do you do with it?
options: leave it in Lanka as a monument.
carry it back to its place in the Himalaya.
keep it for the next emergency.
fork.reveal: he flies it back north and sets it in its place, then returns to the camp.

original.note: Sanskrit mṛtasañjīvanī: the herb that revives the dead, from mṛta, dead, and sañjīvanī, bringing back to life.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman dropped off the mountain and that was the end of it.
what it means: the scent healed the army, and he carried the peak back to where it belonged.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki notes that the rakshasa dead could not rise, because Ravana had them thrown into the sea to hide his losses.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 74 (the herbs' scent heals the army; Ravana's dead in the sea; the peak returned)
Tulsidas, Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kanda (Bharata's arrow and Hanuman at Ayodhya)

notes: Sarga number follows the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Healing by the scent of the herbs, including slain monkeys revived: confirm.
Ravana's order to throw the rakshasa dead into the sea to hide losses: confirm the detail and its placement.
Hanuman returning the peak to the Himalaya in this first episode: confirm.
The Ramcharitmanas episode of Bharata's arrow is placed in the Lanka Kanda; confirm. Some tellings place this herb journey after Lakshmana is struck by Ravana's or Meghanada's spear.
